questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. The ulcer has a clean base, indurated edges and is non-tender. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm and non-tender. The most appropriate diagnostic test is:
questions.exp: Dark field microscopy of serous fluid from the ulcer base is the gold standard for diagnosing primary syphilis, allowing direct visualization of Treponema pallidum spirochetes. VDRL may be negative in early primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with target lesions on her palms, oral erosions and conjunctival involvement following herpes simplex infection 2 weeks ago. She has had three similar episodes in the past. The best long-term management is:
opts: Oral acyclovir 400mg twice daily for 6 months
questions.exp: Recurrent erythema multiforme triggered by HSV is best managed with continuous suppressive antiviral therapy (acyclovir 400mg BD for at least 6 months). This reduces HSV reactivation and subsequent EM episodes.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male from rural India presents with a large hypopigmented macule on the trunk with complete loss of sensation, thickened greater auricular nerve and claw hand deformity. Slit skin smear shows a BI of 5+. The leprosy type is:
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) is characterized by numerous skin lesions, high BI (4+ to 6+), nerve thickening affecting multiple nerves, and deformities like claw hand. Multibacillary disease requires MDT regimen for 12 months.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male presents with flaccid bullae on the trunk and oral erosions. Nikolsky sign is positive. Histopathology shows suprabasal acantholysis. The autoantibody responsible is directed against:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris is characterized by autoantibodies against Desmoglein 3 (mucosal) and sometimes Desmoglein 1 (skin). Mucosal involvement is predominantly due to anti-Dsg3 antibodies. Suprabasal acantholysis is the hallmark histological finding.

questions.q: A 50-year-old female presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin, no oral lesions. Histopathology shows subepidermal bulla with eosinophils. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid shows tense bullae on normal/erythematous skin, subepidermal blisters with eosinophils, and linear IgG+C3 at BMZ on DIF. Autoantibodies are directed against BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female presents with malar erythema, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, arthritis and proteinuria. ANA is positive at 1:640 with a homogeneous pattern. The most specific antibody for this condition is:
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibody is highly specific for SLE (specificity ~99%) though sensitivity is low (25-30%). Anti-dsDNA is also specific and correlates with disease activity, but anti-Sm is the most specific. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with a psoriasiform plaque on the scalp. Wood's lamp examination shows bright green fluorescence. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Microsporum canis (and Microsporum audouinii) produce ectothrix infection with green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Trichophyton species generally do not fluoresce. T. tonsurans and T. violaceum cause endothrix infections.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive male presents with multiple reddish-purple nodules on the skin and oral mucosa. Histopathology shows irregular vascular channels lined by atypical spindle cells with extravasated red blood cells and hyaline globules. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma is caused by Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8/KSHV). It commonly occurs in HIV-positive individuals. The histological findings of irregular vascular channels, spindle cells and hyaline globules are characteristic.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the lower lip for 5 days, with tingling and burning. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The most appropriate treatment for recurrent episodes is:
questions.exp: For frequent recurrences of herpes labialis (>6 episodes/year), suppressive therapy with valacyclovir 500mg OD for 6-12 months reduces frequency by ~80%. Episodic therapy treats individual outbreaks but doesn't prevent recurrences.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male chronic smoker presents with a hard indurated ulcer on the lower lip with everted edges and regional lymphadenopathy. Histopathology shows islands of squamous cells with keratin pearl formation and individual cell keratinization. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma on the lip presents as an indurated ulcer with everted edges. Histologically, it shows squamous differentiation with keratin pearls (concentric layers of squamous cells) and individual cell keratinization. Chronic sun exposure and smoking are major risk factors.

questions.q: A 16-year-old male presents with comedones, papules, pustules and a few nodules on the face and back. His older brother has severe scarring acne. Which of the following best determines the severity and guides treatment in this patient?
opts: Lesion count and distribution using Global Acne Grading System
questions.exp: The Global Acne Grading System (GAGS) or similar validated scoring systems assess lesion type, count and distribution to grade acne severity. This guides appropriate treatment — grade I/II responds to topicals, grade III/IV needs systemic antibiotics or isotretinoin.

questions.q: A 32-year-old female presents with well-defined silvery-white scaly plaques on the elbows and knees with nail pitting and onycholysis. She has a history of joint pain. The pathological hallmark of this condition is:
opts: Elongation of rete ridges with spongiosis
Regular elongation of rete ridges with suprapapillary thinning and Munro microabscesses
questions.exp: Psoriasis histopathology shows regular elongation (clubbing) of rete ridges, suprapapillary thinning of epidermis, parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in stratum corneum), and spongiform pustules of Kogoj.

questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with multiple hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk with peripheral nerve thickening. Lepromin test is strongly positive. Slit skin smear is negative. The WHO MB-MDT regimen for this patient includes:
questions.exp: Even though this patient appears to have paucibacillary (PB) leprosy (negative SSS), WHO now recommends a single regimen: MB-MDT (Dapsone 100mg daily + Rifampicin 600mg monthly + Clofazimine 50mg daily and 300mg monthly) for 12 months, due to concerns about misclassification.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with erythema, scaling and oozing over the scalp, face and trunk for 6 months. KOH examination of skin scrapings is negative. Skin biopsy shows spongiosis with lymphocytic infiltrate. The first-line treatment for seborrhoeic dermatitis affecting the face is:
questions.exp: Topical ketoconazole 2% is first-line for facial seborrhoeic dermatitis as it targets Malassezia (the implicated yeast) and has anti-inflammatory properties. Potent steroids should be avoided on the face due to risk of atrophy, telangiectasia and perioral dermatitis.

questions.q: A 22-year-old female develops erythematous wheals all over the body 30 minutes after eating shellfish. She complains of throat tightness and her BP is 90/60 mmHg. The immediate management is:
opts: IM adrenaline 0.5mg of 1:1000 in the outer thigh
questions.exp: This is anaphylaxis with angioedema and hypotension. IM adrenaline (epinephrine) 0.5mg (0.5ml of 1:1000 solution) in the anterolateral thigh is the immediate life-saving treatment. IV antihistamines and steroids are secondary measures.

questions.q: A 35-year-old female presents with a butterfly-shaped rash on the face, joint pain and hair loss. She is found to have hypocomplementemia (low C3, C4). Which of the following antibodies is most useful for monitoring disease activity?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibody titres correlate with SLE disease activity, particularly lupus nephritis. Rising anti-dsDNA levels often precede flares. Anti-Sm is highly specific but does not correlate with disease activity.

questions.q: A 70-year-old male presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia on the nose. Central ulceration is seen. The histopathological finding expected is:
opts: Keratin pearl formation with individual cell keratinization
Nests of basaloid cells with palisading at the periphery and retraction artifact
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) shows nests and islands of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading of nuclei and retraction artifact (cleft between tumour islands and surrounding stroma). It rarely metastasizes but is locally destructive.

questions.q: A 24-year-old male presents with multiple warty papules over the genitalia. On acetowhitening, lesions become white. Histopathology shows koilocytes and epidermal hyperplasia. The most common causative HPV types for anogenital warts are:
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused predominantly by HPV 6 and 11 (low-risk types). HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk types associated with cervical and other anogenital carcinomas. Koilocytes (vacuolated cells with dark nuclei) are the hallmark of HPV infection.

questions.q: A patient develops widespread erythema, blistering involving >30% BSA, and Nikolsky sign after starting phenytoin 3 weeks ago. Mucous membranes are involved. Mortality risk is approximately:
questions.exp: This is Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) with >30% BSA detachment. TEN carries mortality of 30-50%, calculated by the SCORTEN score. Immediate discontinuation of the causative drug and ICU-level supportive care are essential. IV immunoglobulin and cyclosporine may be used.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male from Bihar presents with a chronic non-healing ulcer on the foot for 2 years with sinus tracts draining yellowish granules. X-ray shows periosteal reaction. The likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Mycetoma (Madura foot) presents with the triad of swelling, sinus tracts, and grains/granules. Yellow granules suggest Madurella mycetomatis or Actinomyces species. X-ray shows periosteal reaction in bony involvement. Treatment depends on whether eumycetoma (antifungals) or actinomycetoma (antibiotics).

questions.q: A 30-year-old female presents with proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, Gottron papules over knuckles and periungual telangiectasia. CPK is elevated. The skin biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis classically presents with heliotrope rash (violaceous periorbital edema), Gottron papules (flat-topped violaceous papules on knuckles), periungual telangiectasia, and proximal muscle weakness with elevated CPK. Skin biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with hardening of the skin on the hands and face, Raynaud phenomenon and difficulty swallowing. Anti-centromere antibody is positive. He likely has:
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc), formerly called CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia). Anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc.

questions.q: A 12-year-old child presents with vesicles on an erythematous base in a dermatomal distribution along T4 for 4 days. Which complication can be prevented by early antiviral therapy?
questions.exp: Post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN) is the most important complication of herpes zoster. Early antiviral therapy (acyclovir/valacyclovir) started within 72 hours of rash onset significantly reduces the incidence and severity of PHN by reducing viral replication and nerve damage.

questions.q: During a Wood's lamp examination in a clinic, which of the following conditions shows coral-red fluorescence?
questions.exp: Erythrasma (caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum) shows characteristic coral-red fluorescence under Wood's lamp due to production of coproporphyrin III. Tinea versicolor shows yellow-green fluorescence and Pseudomonas shows blue-green fluorescence.

questions.q: A 65-year-old male presents with an irregularly pigmented lesion on the back with asymmetry, irregular borders and multiple colors. Dermoscopy shows atypical pigment network and regression structures. The next step in management is:
opts: Excision with 0.5cm margins and await biopsy
Excision with 1cm margins and histopathological examination
Punch biopsy of the darkest area
questions.exp: For suspected melanoma, excisional biopsy with 1-2mm margins (not wide local excision) is the diagnostic procedure of choice. This provides complete histopathological assessment including Breslow thickness, which determines definitive surgical margins. Punch biopsy is acceptable if excision is not feasible.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth for 5 days. Gram stain of the crust shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. The first-line topical treatment is:
questions.exp: Impetigo is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (less commonly Group A Streptococcus). Topical mupirocin 2% is the first-line treatment for localized non-bullous impetigo. It is effective against MRSA as well. Fusidic acid is an alternative.

questions.q: A 38-year-old female presents with pruritic, annular, raised plaques with central clearing on the groin and inner thighs. KOH examination shows branching hyphae. The most appropriate treatment for extensive tinea cruris is:
questions.exp: Extensive tinea cruris (dermatophytosis of groin) requires systemic antifungal therapy. Oral terbinafine 250mg OD for 2-4 weeks is preferred due to its fungicidal activity against dermatophytes. Griseofulvin requires longer duration and has lower cure rates.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male develops palpable purpura on the lower limbs, arthralgias and haematuria. Skin biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits on immunofluorescence. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein Purpura) is characterized by palpable purpura (usually on lower limbs/buttocks), arthritis, abdominal pain and renal involvement, with IgA deposits in vessel walls on immunofluorescence. It is the most common vasculitis in children but also occurs in adults.

questions.q: A drug used in dermatology inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, thereby decreasing purine and pyrimidine synthesis. Which of the following drugs acts by this mechanism?
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking the conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate, which is essential for purine and thymidylate synthesis. This reduces DNA synthesis and cell proliferation. It is used in psoriasis, PV, DM, and other inflammatory conditions.

questions.q: A 30-year-old female presents with multiple, sharply demarcated, well-circumscribed patches of hair loss without visible follicular openings. The patches are smooth and no signs of inflammation. Pull test is positive. Dermatoscopy shows yellow dots, black dots and exclamation mark hairs. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Alopecia areata (AA) shows non-scarring, patchy hair loss with smooth scalp. Dermoscopy reveals yellow dots (empty follicles with sebum), black dots (broken hairs at follicular ostia) and exclamation mark hairs (tapered proximal end). It is an autoimmune condition targeting the hair follicle.

questions.q: A dermatology resident is performing a punch biopsy. She selects a 4mm punch. The depth of the punch biopsy should ideally reach:
opts: Subcutaneous fat to assess inflammation at all levels
questions.exp: A punch biopsy should include epidermis, full dermis and a small amount of subcutaneous fat to allow assessment of all skin layers, adnexal structures and deep inflammatory infiltrates. This is especially important for panniculitis, vasculitis and morphea diagnosis.
